A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dovetail, and their text, figures, tables, and equations support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A–C. Relocated material, including the hardware-effectiveness analysis, can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference-speed, acceptance-length, memory-use, and ablation results for Dovetail, including Tables I–III.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results for 13B models, laptop deployment, timing measurements, and supplementary ablations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains GPU drafting, CPU verification, probability-based draft-tree construction, Dynamic Gated Fusion, and multiple Transformer blocks. The additional model, precision, and hardware configurations do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: ShareGPT training and the MT-bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, and Alpaca evaluation tasks are retained. v2 additionally tests a constrained personal-computer deployment with an i5-9300H and 4GB GTX 1050 Mobile, extending the two Xeon-server scenarios evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: The principal comparators remain EAGLE-2, TinyLlama, ShearedLlama, SpecExec, CPU-only inference, and offloading. v2 Table 4 adds reported Offload comparisons on HumanEval, where v1 Table II had blank entries. Table 5 also introduces a GPTQ-4bit Offload comparator for the laptop experiment.

E3.justification: The reported training configuration changes from four A800 GPUs and 50 epochs to eight A800 GPUs and 24 epochs; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun. Evaluation adds LLaMA2-Chat 13B and Vicuna 13B, plus laptop settings using an int8 target, tree depth 4, and seven candidates, compared with depth 7 and 16 candidates on servers.

E4.justification: The original candidate-count sensitivity analysis and 7B ablations are retained. v2 adds hardware and stage-timing measurements, Vicuna 13B DGF/depth ablations on RTX 2080 and GTX 1050, and a SpecExec comparison using 16 versus 128 candidates (Tables 1 and 7–10). These examine deployment bottlenecks and the justification for comparator settings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional averages and timing measurements in v2 retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: The shared 7B benchmark and ablation values are retained, while substantial new result blocks appear. Examples include Vicuna 13B's 2.65x mean speedup at temperature 0 in Table 3, LLaMA2-Chat 13B HumanEval speedups of 10.14x for Dovetail versus 7.10x for SpecExec in Table 4, and quantized Vicuna 13B laptop throughput of 3.36 tokens/second in Table 5. These concern newly reported configurations.

T1.justification: v1 Equations 1–5 are retained as v2 Appendix B Equations 2–6, and v1 Equation 6 becomes v2 Equation 1. The latency model, overlap assumptions, and hardware-effectiveness inequality remain substantively unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The heterogeneous-decoding and draft-model contributions remain the same. The abstract shifts its quantitative emphasis from 7B throughput under 3–7GB VRAM to 13B speedups of approximately 1.79–10.1x across devices, and the introduction adds the 10.14x result to its contribution statement.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes accelerating a quantized target from preserving its pre-quantization accuracy. Appendix C.2 attributes the laptop's slowdown with an extra draft block to the int8-target/fp16-draft timing relationship and suggests quantizing the draft. The earlier long-prefill limitation and hardware-imbalance qualification are retained.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands configuration documentation through exact CPU/GPU layer allocations, laptop hardware and PyTorch dynamic-quantization details, and SpecExec draft-model and candidate-count settings. Training hardware and duration are revised from four GPUs and approximately 4–5 days to eight GPUs and approximately one day. The code link is retained, although v1's explicit 128GB server-RAM specification is omitted.

R1.justification: The research positioning remains largely stable. Citations are added for works including EAGLE, TinyLlama, KIVI, and lossless compression, while LLM.int8, SpinQuant, and Blockwise Parallel Decoding are removed. Changes to MagicDec and Judge Decoding references concern the same works' publication metadata.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, methods, experiments, and related work are rewritten or condensed. The effectiveness analysis moves into Appendix B, the naming illustration moves into Appendix A, and limitations receive a separate section. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and table styling, expands the opening speedup chart to three deployment configurations, and adds hardware, timing, laptop, and supplementary-analysis tables. Architecture diagrams are restyled, the sensitivity plot gains separate axes, and v1's generic speculative-decoding illustration is removed. Other illustrations are relocated.

improvement.justification: v1's broad consumer-device claims were evaluated with one 7B target on Xeon servers. v2 substantially strengthens their empirical basis through 13B targets and an actual constrained laptop, including evidence that additional draft depth can hurt performance. Added SpecExec controls and deployment details improve interpretability and reproducibility. The unexplained training-budget revision alongside unchanged 7B results remains a reporting weakness, but the expanded validation provides a substantial net improvement.
